Lesson 11.1 · 45 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Capstone: trace one compliant loan end to end

After this lesson you can:
  • Run a synthetic application through consent, KYC, decision, KFS, sanction and disbursement
  • Name the control and the evidence at each gate as you pass it
  • Follow the account into servicing, delinquency and closure paths
On this page
  1. The exercise
  2. What you should be able to say afterwards
  3. Where this lives in LoanOS
  4. Knowledge check

1. The exercise

Everything in this course converges on one traceable journey. In the sandbox (synthetic borrowers only — that boundary is itself a control), run the Guide's *first compliant loan* exercise and narrate each step in this course's terms:

  1. Consent — purpose-bound entries appear in the consent ledger (module 2).
  2. KYC — the record reaches a verified state with evidence; Aadhaar artefacts conspicuously absent (module 2).
  3. Decision — verified facts meet a versioned policy in the engine; note the reason codes and lineage (module 3). Resolve one referral through the workflow, not around it.
  4. KFS — generate, deliver, accept; try to levy an undisclosed charge and watch it fail (module 4).
  5. Sanction and packet — conditions, validity, eSign evidence, vault receipt (module 4).
  6. Disbursement — the readiness checklist goes green; maker-checker authorises; the account opens (modules 4–5).
  7. Servicing — schedule, statement, a simulated payment posting through the waterfall (module 5).
  8. The stress path — simulate a missed instalment: DPD starts, the account enters a bucket, a collections task derives (module 6, module 7).
  9. Evidence — export the scoped evidence pack and verify chain integrity (module 9).

2. What you should be able to say afterwards

The exit bar for this course is a narrative test. For any step, you can answer: which regulation demands this (register family ID), which control implements it (capability ID or module), what evidence it left (audit event, document, ledger entry), and what would have happened on failure (the fail-closed path). If any answer is fuzzy, the relevant module lesson is one click away.

Remember the boundary the Guide states plainly: completing the sandbox exercise is onboarding evidence — it does not, by itself, make anything production-ready.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — The journey you trace is the directions' conduct model made executable.
  • RBI-KFS-2024 — The KFS gate you exercise mid-journey.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Operating guide first-compliant-loan (open in the Guide) — The Guide's guided exercise this capstone wraps.
  • Operating guide evidence-pack (open in the Guide) — Export and verify the evidence pack at the end.
  • App surface /dashboard/ — Staff workspace where the journey's tasks surface.
  • Document docs/operations/demo-handbook.md — Showcase operating model — the same journey, presented.

Key terms

Knowledge check

1. Why must the capstone use synthetic borrowers?

  1. Real data is slow
  2. The sandbox enforces synthetic-only borrowers — using production personal data in training is itself a data-protection violation
  3. Licensing costs
  4. No reason; it's convention
Show answer

B. Training and evaluation happen in the sandbox boundary precisely so personal data never leaks into learning exercises.

2. Completing the capstone proves…

  1. The tenant is production-ready
  2. You can trace and explain the governed journey — an onboarding outcome, not a production attestation
  3. The policies are correct
  4. Nothing
Show answer

B. The maturity language is deliberate: sandbox completion is learning evidence; production readiness has its own, separate gates.
